Real-World Imprinting Analysis: GSE52576 Dataset

Source: vignettes/articles/GSE52576.Rmd
GSE52576.Rmd

Download, preprocess, and analyze methylation data from a public GEO dataset

Overview

This vignette demonstrates imprintomeR on GSE52576, a real-world methylation dataset from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO). You will:

  1. Download normalized beta values from GEO using GEOquery
  2. Create an ImprintomeSet analysis-ready object
  3. Analyze imprinting status across samples
  4. Visualize results with all available plot types
  5. Interpret biological patterns and aberrant imprinting
  6. Compare scoring options: DMR type, bootstrap intervals, ICR-balanced and per-ICR scores, and locus panels

The workflow is optimized for reproducibility and Jupyter notebook conversion.

Phase 1: Setup & Data Download

Load libraries 

library(imprintomeR)
library(GEOquery)
library(tidyverse)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

# For reproducibility
set.seed(2026)

Download GSE52576 from GEO

GSE52576 is a publicly available dataset of Genome-wide parent-of-origin DNA methylation analysis using Illumina 450K methylation arrays.

# Download GSE52576 from GEO
geo_gse <- "GSE52576"
message("Downloading ", geo_gse, " from GEO...")

tryCatch({
  gse <- getGEO(geo_gse, GSEMatrix = TRUE, AnnotGPL = TRUE, getGPL = FALSE)
  eset <- gse[[1]]  # Extract ExpressionSet object

  message("✓ Download successful")
  message("  Samples: ", ncol(eset))
  message("  Probes:  ", nrow(eset))
}, error = function(e) {
  stop("Failed to download ", geo_gse, ":\n", conditionMessage(e),
       "\nCheck internet connection and GEO availability.")
})

Extract metadata and beta values 

# Extract phenotype data (metadata)
pdata <- pData(eset)
message("Available metadata columns:")
print(colnames(pdata))

# Display sample information
message("\nSample overview:")
head(pdata[, c("geo_accession", "title", "source_name_ch1")], n = 3)

Format data for imprintomeR 

# Extract beta values (methylation intensities, 0-1 scale)
beta_matrix <- exprs(eset)
message("Beta matrix dimensions: ", nrow(beta_matrix), " probes × ",
        ncol(beta_matrix), " samples")
message("Beta range: [", round(min(beta_matrix, na.rm = TRUE), 3), ", ",
        round(max(beta_matrix, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "]")

# Create metadata data.frame compatible with imprintomeR
meta <- data.frame(
  Sample_Name = colnames(beta_matrix),
  Sample_Group = pdata$source_name_ch1,  # Disease status or tissue type
  Disease_Status = pdata$characteristics_ch1.1,  # Detailed phenotype
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Clean up Sample_Group (shorten for readability)
meta$Sample_Group <- gsub("^.*: ", "", meta$Sample_Group)

message("\nMetadata created:")
message("Samples: ", nrow(meta))
print(table(meta$Sample_Group))

message("\nFirst few samples:")
head(meta, n = 3)

Validate data integrity 

# Check for missing values
pct_missing <- colSums(is.na(beta_matrix)) / nrow(beta_matrix) * 100
message("Missing values per sample:")
if (max(pct_missing) > 0) {
  print(head(sort(pct_missing, decreasing = TRUE)))
} else {
  message("  ✓ No missing values")
}

# Verify sample name alignment
if (all(colnames(beta_matrix) == meta$Sample_Name)) {
  message("✓ Sample names aligned between beta and metadata")
} else {
  stop("Sample name mismatch!")
}

Phase 2: Load & Create ImprintomeSet

Load data using imprintomeR utilities 

# Use imprintomeR's LoadMetaBeta function to validate and intersect data
beta <- as.data.frame(beta_matrix)
beta <- cbind(NAME = rownames(beta), beta)
input <- LoadMetaBeta(meta, beta, probeset = NULL)

message("Loaded data:")
message("  Samples: ", ncol(input$beta))
message("  Probes:  ", nrow(input$beta))
message("  Metadata cols: ", paste(colnames(input$meta), collapse = ", "))

# Peek at data structure
message("\nBeta matrix (first 5 probes, 3 samples):")
print(round(input$beta[1:5, 1:3], 3))

Create ImprintomeSet object 

# Load probeset annotations
probesets <- readRDS(
  system.file("extdata", "probesets_hg38.rds", package = "imprintomeR")
)

# Create analysis-ready ImprintomeSet
x <- ImprintomeSet(
  beta = input$beta,
  meta = input$meta,
  probeset = probesets[["selected"]],  # Use all probes; will be subset by runImprintome
  genome = "hg38",
  assay = "450K"  # GSE52576 uses Illumina 450K (close to EPIC v1)
)

# Verify object structure
message("ImprintomeSet created:")
message("  Samples: ", ncol(beta(x)))
message("  Probes: ", nrow(beta(x)))
message("  Genome: ", x@genome)
message("  Assay: ", x@assay)
print(summary(x))

Phase 3: Run Workflow & Compute Statistics

Execute imprintomeR analysis 

message("Running imprintome analysis...")
x <- runImprintome(x)
message("Analysis complete")

# Extract results
res <- results(x)
message("\nResults available:")
print(names(res))

# Display analysis summary
message("\nAnalysis summary:")
status <- res$AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected
print(head(status,n=5))

Compute per-group statistics 

# Summarize by Sample_Group
message("\nImprinting status by group:")
print(table(status[, c("Sample_Group", "Status")]))

Review key metrics 

# Distribution of key imprinting metrics
message("IDS (Imprinting Defect Score) distribution:")
print(summary(status$IDS))

message("\nStatus classification:")
print(table(status$Status))

message("\nAngle (parental origin deviation) distribution:")
print(summary(status$Angle))

Phase 4: Visualizations - Complete Gallery

message("Representative sample for single-sample plots: ", sample_id_1)

x <- runImprintomeVisualizations(

  sample_id = sample_id_1,
  prefix = "GSE52576",
  store_plots = TRUE,
  save_plots = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE

attr(x, "visualization_manifest")

Display selected stored plots

}

}

rainfall_name <- grep("^rainfall\\.", names(plots(x)), value = TRUE)[1]

}

Phase 5: Results Interpretation & Case Study

Summary statistics 

res <- results(x)
status <- res$AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected
normal_n <- sum(status$Status %in% "Normal", na.rm = TRUE)
total_n <- nrow(status)
normal_pct <- normal_n / total_n * 100
abnormal_pct <- 100 - normal_pct

message("=== OVERALL IMPRINTING SUMMARY ===")
message(sprintf("Normal imprinting:   %6.1f%% (%d/%d samples)",
                normal_pct, normal_n, total_n))
message(sprintf("Altered imprinting:  %6.1f%% (%d/%d samples)",
                abnormal_pct, total_n - normal_n, total_n))

message("\n=== BY SAMPLE GROUP ===")
if ("Sample_Group" %in% colnames(status)) {
  for (group in unique(status$Sample_Group)) {
    idx <- status$Sample_Group == group
    n <- sum(idx, na.rm = TRUE)
    normal <- sum(status$Status[idx] == "Normal", na.rm = TRUE)
    message(sprintf("%20s: %d samples, %d normal (%.1f%%)",
                    group, n, normal, 100 * normal / n))
  }
} else {
  message("Sample_Group column not available in status table.")
}

Identify samples with altered imprinting 

abnormal <- status %>% filter(!Status %in% "Normal")
sample_col <- intersect(c("Sample_Name", "Sample_ID"), colnames(status))[1]

if (nrow(abnormal) > 0) {
  message("=== ALTERED IMPRINTING SAMPLES ===")
  message("Sample count: ", nrow(abnormal))
  cols_to_show <- c(sample_col, intersect("Sample_Group", colnames(abnormal)),
                    "Status", "IDS", "Angle")
  print(abnormal %>% select(all_of(cols_to_show)) %>% head(n = 12))
} else {
  message("All samples show normal imprinting patterns by the selected IDS cutoff.")
}

Phenotype-imprinting associations 

if ("Sample_Group" %in% colnames(status) && length(unique(status$Sample_Group)) > 1) {
  message("Cross-tabulation: Sample_Group vs Imprinting Status")
  tbl <- table(status$Sample_Group, status$Status)
  print(tbl)

  group_summary <- status %>%
    group_by(Sample_Group, Status) %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      median_IDS = median(IDS, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_Angle = median(Angle, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  print(group_summary)
} else {
  message("Sample_Group is unavailable or has one level; skipping group cross-tabulation.")
}

Key findings 

message("=== KEY BIOLOGICAL INSIGHTS ===")
message("1. Dataset: GSE52576, methylation study of imprinting disorders")
message("2. Platform: Illumina HumanMethylation450K")
message("3. Samples analyzed: ", total_n)
message("4. IDS range: [",
        round(min(status$IDS, na.rm = TRUE), 3), ", ",
        round(max(status$IDS, na.rm = TRUE), 3), "]")
message("5. Most common imprinting status: ",
        names(sort(table(status$Status), decreasing = TRUE))[1])
message("6. Compare Sample_Group summaries above to relate imprinting status to phenotype groups.")

Phase 6: Scoring Options

The sections above use the package defaults: the selected panel scored on gametic ICRs against the fixed 0.5 reference. This phase shows the other scoring options on the same data. Each call adds a result table to results(x) under its own name, so earlier results are kept.

GSE52576 has no tissue-matched control group, so all scores here use the fixed 0.5 reference.

Gametic ICRs, all probes and secondary DMRs

runImprintome() scores the core selected panel on gametic ICRs by default (dmr_type = "gametic"). dmr_type = "all" scores every probe, as in earlier package versions, and dmr_type = "secondary" scores the secondary DMRs separately.

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", dmr_type = "all")
x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", dmr_type = "secondary")
res <- results(x)

scored <- c(gametic    = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected",
            all_probes = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.all",
            secondary  = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.secondary")

# Probes per parental class for each selection
t(sapply(scored, function(nm) unlist(res[[nm]][1, c("n_paternal_probes", "n_maternal_probes")])))

# Mechanism of each sample under each selection
mechanism_by_selection <- data.frame(
  Sample_Name  = status$Sample_Name,
  Sample_Group = status$Sample_Group,
  sapply(scored, function(nm) res[[nm]]$Mechanism[match(status$Sample_Name, res[[nm]]$Sample_Name)])
)
mechanism_by_selection[order(mechanism_by_selection$Sample_Group), ]

The gametic paternal class is essentially the H19/IGF2 IG-DMR, so report n_paternal_probes alongside gametic scores.

Bootstrap uncertainty intervals

n_boot adds percentile intervals for IDS and Angle from a two-stage bootstrap (ICRs, then probes within ICRs), and Mechanism_support, the fraction of replicates that fall in the reported sector. Use at least 1,000 replicates for reporting; 200 keep this example fast.

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", n_boot = 200, seed = 2026,
                   result_name = "AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.boot")
boot <- results(x)[["AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.boot"]]
boot[, c("Sample_Name", "Sample_Group", "IDS", "IDS_lower", "IDS_upper",
         "Angle", "Angle_lower", "Angle_upper", "Mechanism", "Mechanism_support")]

The intervals are conditional on the reference (with in-cohort controls, resample_reference = TRUE includes its uncertainty). The origin permutation test (n_perm) is interpretable only for scores centred on control samples (reference_group), and CalibrateIDS() needs tissue-matched controls, so neither is shown here.

ICR-balanced IDS and per-ICR calls

The sample-level IDS pools all probes of a parental class, so probe-rich ICRs dominate it. balance = "icr" takes the median within each ICR and then across ICRs, so that each ICR counts once. icr = TRUE also scores each ICR on its own and summarizes the altered ICRs per sample.

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "selected", balance = "icr", icr = TRUE)
res <- results(x)

# Probe-pooled versus ICR-balanced IDS
balanced <- res[["AnalyzeImprintStatus.selected.icr"]]
data.frame(Sample_Name      = status$Sample_Name,
           Sample_Group     = status$Sample_Group,
           IDS_pooled       = status$IDS,
           IDS_icr_balanced = balanced$IDS[match(status$Sample_Name, balanced$Sample_Name)])

# Per-ICR table (one row per sample and ICR) and per-sample summary
icr_table   <- res[["ICRStatus.selected"]]
icr_summary <- res[["ICRSummary.selected"]]
table(icr_table$DMR_type[!duplicated(icr_table$ICR_name)])   # ICRs scored, by DMR type
icr_summary[, c("Sample_Name", "Sample_Group", "n_icrs", "n_altered", "n_gain", "n_loss",
                "n_altered_chromosomes", "MLID")]

# Count gametic ICRs only
SummarizeICRStatus(icr_table, dmr_type = "gametic")[, c("Sample_Name", "n_icrs", "n_altered", "MLID")]

Per-ICR calls cover all annotated ICRs, secondary DMRs included. The call thresholds (|deviation| ≥ 0.175 and |z| ≥ 2) were selected and evaluated with control samples. GSE52576 has normal tissues but no control group matched to the other samples’ tissue. Without controls, z is unavailable and only the deviation criterion applies, so tissue-specific methylation is called altered. Note how many ICRs are called altered in samples expected to be normal. Treat these calls as exploratory, or rerun with controls from the same study (reference_group), or with a larger delta_cutoff such as 0.25.

Locus panels: chr11p15 and chr20q13 (GNAS)

Locus panels give a two-axis IDS/Angle for a single imprinted domain: IC1 and IC2 at 11p15.5 (chr11p15), and GNAS-NESP against the maternal GNAS DMRs at 20q13 (chr20q13).

x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "chr11p15")
x <- runImprintome(x, probeset = "chr20q13")
res <- results(x)

do.call(rbind, lapply(c("chr11p15", "chr20q13"), function(p) {
  res[[paste0("AnalyzeImprintStatus.", p)]] %>%
    group_by(Sample_Group) %>%
    summarise(panel = p, n = n(), median_IDS = round(median(IDS), 3), max_IDS = round(max(IDS), 3),
              .groups = "drop")
}))

Per-ICR heatmap

The icr_heatmap plot type draws the stored per-ICR table, samples by ICRs; non-gametic ICRs are marked with *. runImprintomeVisualizations() includes it in the default set whenever runImprintome(..., icr = TRUE) has been run.

x <- runImprintomeVisualizations(
  x,
  plot_types = "icr_heatmap",
  probeset = "selected",
  prefix = "GSE52576_icr_heatmap",
  store_plots = TRUE,
  save_plots = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)
options(repr.plot.width = 12, repr.plot.height = 8)
print(plots(x)[["icr_heatmap.selected"]])
names(results(x))

Phase 7: Export Results 

manifest <- export(
  x,
  outdir = "GSE52576_imprintome_output",
  prefix = "GSE52576",
  save_plots = TRUE,
  plot_device = "pdf",
  overwrite = TRUE
)

head(manifest)

export() writes the full ImprintomeSet object as <prefix>_imprintomeSet.rds, plus results(x) and optionally plots(x). Save extra summary tables only when you need custom reporting beyond the export manifest.

Jupyter Notebook Conversion Guide

A run copy of this guide as a notebook, with outputs, is tutorials/GSE52576.ipynb. This guide is plain Markdown (code blocks are shown, not run, on the website); each R code block is one notebook cell. To create a notebook with an R kernel:

jupytext --from md --to notebook --set-kernel ir vignettes/articles/GSE52576.Rmd

Tips for Jupyter users: - Run the raw-IDAT download and QC cells only when you need full preprocessing; they download a large archive. - Save the downloaded GEO and IDAT files once and reuse them, rather than downloading in every session. - Set outFile in plot calls to save publication-ready PDFs or PNGs. - End with local({ si <- sessionInfo(); si$BLAS <- basename(si$BLAS); si$LAPACK <- basename(si$LAPACK); si }) so that saved notebooks do not record local library paths.
